notes:
Account overview:
- Legacy media archive: news footage transcripts, program guides, user-submitted annotations. Documents are long (10k-50k words) and noisy OCR in places.
- Primary problem: relevance for producer/editor search and fast retrieval for re-use/licensing. Current Elastic cluster struggling with recall/precision on long docs.
- Scale: target index 120k assets for POC (~600k chunks), eventual full set ~1.5M assets => estimated 5-8M chunks depending on chunk size.
Technical requirements and preferences:
- Retrieval architecture considered: hybrid approach (dense vector retrieval for recall + sparse BM25 filter for recall precision). Customer favors embeddings + reranker flow: bi-encoder for ANN then cross-encoder rerank top-50.
- Reranker candidates: prefer a distilled cross-encoder (e.g., smaller T5 cross-encoder) to keep latency low; willing to test Redwood's hosted reranker or bring their own transformer.
- Chunking: experimenting with semantic chunking (paragraph-level + overlap) vs fixed 2-3k token chunks. Trade-offs discussed: larger chunks reduce ANN entries but increase per-vector compute and potentially reduce reranker effectiveness; smaller chunks raise storage and ANN memory costs.
- Metadata strategy: keep canonical ids, timestamp, show/episode, speaker labels; plan to store chunk-level offsets to reconstruct context for summarization.
- Latency SLOs: interactive editor search target 150-250ms median to first-pass results; acceptable total time to page with rerank ~500ms for web UI. Batch archival search can be higher.
- Cost goals: target amortized query cost < $0.01 for retrieval+rerank in production; POC budget allows higher during experimentation.
- Indexing cadence: nightly full refresh for new ingest; ability to reindex specific shows on demand. Need CDC-friendly pipeline.
POC plan and metrics:
- POC dataset: 120k assets from 2016-2022 (news + documentaries). Split by show; build baseline embeddings with OpenAI-style Ada-ish vector, then test Redwood-verified small/quantized models.
- Evaluation metrics: MRR@10, nDCG@5, precision@1 for editorial queries; human eval tags (useful/irrelevant) from 50 editors. Also measure median latency, 95th pct latency, cost/query.
- Reranker tuning: plan grid sweep on positive/negative sampling (hard negatives from BM25 and in-batch negatives), learning rate schedule, and top-k size for re-ranking (test top-20, top-50, top-100). Will instrument eval harness to detect regression vs baseline.
- Caching: heavy prefix caching for common show/episode queries; hope to reduce reranker invocation for repeated queries.
Operational concerns discussed:
- ANN sizing: estimate for 5M chunks using HNSW requires dedicated nodes; customer interested in Dedicated GPU pool for cross-encoder reranks and for batched scoring.
- Quantization and model selection: prefer 8-bit quantized bi-encoder for retrieval; float16 cross-encoder in dedicated capacity. Discussed Redwood Optimize recommendations for quantization profiles.
- Failover policies: when Dedicated capacity constrained, fall back to smaller reranker or skip rerank entirely with clear UX degrade. They liked Redwood's routing/fallback ideas.
